description: The Mission at Kern County provides meals and services in Bakersfield, with overnight shelter described for men. Meal access and shelter intake are separate questions.
introduction: The Mission at Kern County provides meals and services in Bakersfield, with overnight shelter described for men. Meal access and shelter intake are separate questions.

who: The Mission says anyone in the community can receive a hot meal. Its homeless-services page describes overnight shelter for men; ask staff about eligibility and available space for the service you need.
sections.get: Services include meals, clothing and support referrals. Residents can access hygiene facilities and other listed support. Program access and schedules should be confirmed with staff.
sections.docs: For a meal, ask the information booth where to go. For shelter, explain your circumstances and ask about intake, identification, arrival time and belongings; do not assume a meal visit reserves a bed.
sections.apply: Check in at the information booth at 816 East 21st Street, Bakersfield, as directed by the Mission’s homeless services page. Ask staff for current meal and shelter instructions.
sections.after: Clarify the next visit or overnight requirements and ask about housing and benefits referrals. If the shelter cannot serve your household, contact 211 for another placement option.

faqs: Can someone outside the shelter receive a meal?
The provider says anyone in the community can receive a hot meal.
Is the overnight shelter described for all households?
The inspected page describes men’s overnight shelter. Ask about alternatives for other households.
Does a meal guarantee a bed?
No. Ask separately about shelter intake and available space.
Why are exact dinner hours not listed here?
The provider’s dinner time contains a typographical error; confirm the current schedule with staff.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
